The case for the Multiple Realisability of Agency over the Artificial Realisability of Intelligence is announced (evidence, common sense, Ockham, literature) and then set aside: the paper assumes AI is an agent and asks what kind (p. 2). Floridi & Sanders' three criteria come back, loosened, so that interactivity alone makes a river a "natural agent" (p. 9). The criteria do not separate AI from other artefacts. Origin, mechanism, where the goals come from, and asserted absences (no intelligence, no mental states) do that. No level of abstraction is ever specified. | Read |
| [NOTE-703](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-703.md) | Forssten et al. — One Giant Leap from Mouse to Man | A narrative review, by employees of a probiotics manufacturer, of the microbiota–gut–brain axis in mood. The routes in rodents are well documented. Faecal transplant from depressed humans partly transfers the phenotype to rodents. Human trials are mixed: some reductions in subjective stress in healthy volunteers, and several clean nulls for strains with strong preclinical records. It documents its own translational failures and ends more optimistically than they warrant. | Read |
| [NOTE-704](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-704.md) | Simon — The Architecture of Complexity | Complexity usually takes the form of hierarchy, defined by intensity of interaction rather than subordination. Hierarchies evolve fast because stable intermediate forms survive interruption, and they are nearly decomposable: fast, nearly independent dynamics inside subsystems; slow, aggregate dynamics between them. The theorem is cited, not shown; the evolutionary numbers are illustrative; the social claims are asserted. | Read |
| [NOTE-705](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-705.md) | Orseau, McGill & Legg — Agents and Devices | A formal counterpart of Dennett's physical and intentional stances. A device is a mixture of input-output mappings; an agent is a mixture of goal-optimizing ε-greedy policies, by inverse RL. Bayes' rule gives the posterior probability that a system is an agent. It is illustrated in a toy gridworld, with no human comparison. Agency is explicitly relative to the observer's prior. A clearly identified system is assumed. | Read |
| [NOTE-706](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-706.md) | Han et al. — From gut microbiota to host appetite | A narrative review, not systematic, by animal-nutrition scientists, of how gut-microbe metabolites and proteins may regulate host appetite. The mechanisms are plausible and mostly shown in rodents. The human evidence is associations in eating disorders and obesity, and prebiotic or metabolite trials that conflict across populations and durations. The authors say so. The framing is mutualist: no microbe "interest" in host eating is argued. | Read |
| [NOTE-707](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-707.md) | Kenton et al. — Discovering Agents | An interventional, causal definition of agents. Mechanised causal models add a mechanism variable for each object-level variable. Decision nodes are found as variables whose mechanisms respond to downstream mechanisms (terminal edges), and utility nodes as the targets of those responses. Recovery of the true game graph is proved under five assumptions, including interventional data on mechanisms. The verdicts are sensible. The labels are frame-dependent and granularity-sensitive, which the paper states but does not treat as a threat. | Read |
| [NOTE-708](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-708.md) | Vekilov — Nucleation | For lysozyme, measured homogeneous nucleation rates of crystals from solution are about ten orders of magnitude below the classical prediction, level off as supersaturation rises, and pass through a maximum as temperature falls. The paper explains these by two things classical theory lacks. A solution–crystal spinodal, defined kinetically as where the nucleus shrinks to one molecule, so the barrier vanishes. And a two-step mechanism, in which crystals nucleate inside metastable clusters of dense liquid that form fast; ordering inside the clusters is the slow step. For metastable clusters the two-step mechanism is inferred from a kinetic model fitted to one protein's data, not observed. The evidence for other systems is weaker and the author grades it so. The paper also argues that near the spinodal the barrier is negligible, so heterogeneous substrates must act on the prefactor, not the barrier. | Read |
| [NOTE-709](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-709.md) | Ostwald — Studies on the formation and transformation of solids, I | Ostwald times how small a crystal fragment can be and still seed a supercooled melt or supersaturated solution (down to about 10⁻⁹–10⁻¹² g). He shows that only the solid substance itself, or a strictly isomorphous solid, seeds. He divides states beyond equilibrium into metastable ones, which change only on contact with the other phase, and labile ones, where the new phase forms spontaneously. In §§32–41 he states the rule later called the rule of stages: on leaving a state, the form reached is "not the most stable ... but the nearest" (pp. 306–307), meaning the form with the next-highest free energy. He offers it "not as a law" but as "a frequently applicable rule" (p. 308), drawn from experience and backed by an analogy with the van der Waals isotherm. The rule covers spontaneous formation only. Whether a metastable intermediate goes on to the next form depends on whether it is labile with respect to it; if it is merely metastable it stays until seeded (p. 308). The word "Stufenregel" does not appear in the paper. | Read |
| [NOTE-711](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-711.md) | The Limiting Dynamics of SGD | SGD with momentum β, learning rate η, batch size S and weight decay λ is modelled as (η/2)(1 + β)θ̈ + (1 − β)θ̇ + λθ = −g(θ) + √(η/S) √Σ ξ(t). For linear regression with Σ = σ²H this is an OU process in phase space. Its stationary state is Gibbs on a modified loss, with inverse temperature κ = S(1 − β²), in broken detailed balance. Under a quadratic loss at the end of training the same holds for deep networks, and a ResNet-18 on ImageNet shows the predicted isotropy, velocity regularization, oscillations and speed. | Read |
| [NOTE-712](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-712.md) | Symmetry in Neural Network Parameter Spaces | A symmetry is a group action on parameters preserving the network function (Def. 2.4) or the loss (Def. 2.6), possibly only on given data or in expectation (Defs. 2.8–2.9). Common components have GL, scaling, sign-flip, orthogonal, translation and permutation symmetries (Table 1). Continuous symmetries make minima connected manifolds, and give gradient flow conserved quantities that label trajectories and endpoints (§5). SGD's finite steps, noise and weight decay break these, which is an open route to implicit bias (§7.2). | Read |
| [NOTE-713](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-713.md) | Neural Mechanics | A symmetry ψ of the loss gives ⟨∇L, ∂_α ψ⟩ = 0 and a Hessian constraint. Under gradient flow, Theorem 1 conserves ⟨θ, ∂_α ψ⟩: for translation ⟨θ_A, 1⟩, for scale \|θ_A\|², for rescale \|θ_A1\|² − \|θ_A2\|². With weight decay λ and the modified loss L + (η/4)\|∇L\|², these become exponentially decaying memories plus integrals of gradient norms (Eqs. 18–20), matched on VGG-16 with Tiny ImageNet. The noise covariance annihilates the generators (§5, App. F). | Read |
| [NOTE-714](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-714.md) | Noise Balance and Stationary Distribution of Stochastic Gradient Descent | SDE: dθ = −∇L dt + √(T C(θ)) dW, with T = η/S. With ℓ(u, w) = ℓ(λu, w/λ), d(‖u‖² − ‖w‖²)/dt = −T(uᵀC₁u − wᵀC₂w) (Theorem 1). The stationary point is Tr C(w) = Tr C(u). With weight decay γ the rate is TC₀ + γ (Corollary 2.1). Diagonal linear network ℓ = (Σᵢ ∏ₖ u_i^{(k)} x − y)²: sign coherence and balance for depth D > 1 (Theorem 3), exact stationary distribution (Theorem 4), collapse above T_c = β₂/α₃ for D = 1, tail ∝ v^{−5+3/(D+1)} independent of data. | Read |
| [NOTE-715](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-715.md) | From Lazy to Rich: Exact Learning Dynamics in Deep Linear Networks | Two-layer linear network ŷ = W₂W₁x, MSE, full-batch gradient flow. Assumptions: whitened inputs (A1), λ-balanced start W₂ᵀW₂ − W₁W₁ᵀ = λI (A2), no bottleneck (A3). Then QQᵀ, with Q = [W₁ᵀ; W₂], obeys a matrix Riccati equation (Lemma 4.1), solved exactly (Theorem 4.3). For aligned starts, each singular value moves by a λ-dependent transition function: sigmoidal as λ → 0, exponential 1 − e^{−\|λ\|t/τ} as \|λ\| → ∞ (Theorem 5.1). | Read |
| [NOTE-716](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-716.md) | Symmetry Induces Structure and Constraint of Learning | ℓ_γ = ℓ₀(θ, x) + γ‖θ‖². O-mirror symmetry: ℓ₀(θ) = ℓ₀((I − 2OOᵀ)θ). Theorem 1: (1) Oᵀθ = 0 implies Oᵀ∇ℓ_γ = 0; (2) at symmetric points the Hessian splits into ker(Oᵀ) and im(OOᵀ) blocks; (3) above some γ₀ the projection (I − OOᵀ)θ has lower loss; (4) above some γ₁ all minima satisfy Oᵀθ = 0. SGD near the symmetric set: Pθ_{t+1} = Pθ_t − λH(x)Pθ_t, attractive when the Lyapunov exponent E log\|1 − λ(ξ + γ)\| < 0. Corollaries: sparsity, low rank, homogeneous neurons (Theorems 2–4). | Read |
| [NOTE-717](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-717.md) | Kamenica & Gentzkow — Bayesian Persuasion | With a common prior and a sender who commits to a signal the receiver sees, any distribution of posteriors whose mean is the prior can be induced, so the sender's best value is the concave closure of its posterior-value function at the prior (Corollary 2). A fully informed, fully rational receiver can be moved; at the optimum she is indifferent whenever she acts for the sender. The paper never cites Blackwell, does not analyse manipulation, and has the receiver know the design. | Read |
| [NOTE-718](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-718.md) | Gallego & Orús — Language Design as Information Renormalization | Reads Chomsky's MERGE as a coarse-graining and builds sentence probabilities as mostly loop-free tensor networks of 3-index MERGE tensors, one per node of a given parse. Because MERGE's output is fixed by its input, a parsed sentence's probability is a product of local coefficients. Tree-shaped parses make correlations decay with tree distance, about log \|j − i\|, so polynomially in word separation. The averaging step that turns this into a claim about languages is asserted, and nothing is tested on data. Syntax only: semantics and context are set aside by the authors. | Read |
| [NOTE-719](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-719.md) v2 | Di Paolo — Autopoiesis, Adaptivity, Teleology, Agency | Autopoiesis, read as conservation, gives only an all-or-nothing norm that an observer can see and the system cannot use. Sense-making needs adaptivity in addition: a graded capacity to monitor and regulate tendencies toward the viability boundary, which yields good, neutral and bad ways of staying alive for the system itself. Agency is the regulation of coupling with the environment, not coupling itself. The argument is conceptual, with one footnoted model (the Chemoton), and the closing section on non-metabolic values is declared speculative. | Read |
| [NOTE-720](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-720.md) v2 | Weber & Varela — Life after Kant | An argument, not a model: Kant's natural purposes (§§ 64–65), Jonas's metabolism and Maturana and Varela's autopoiesis converge on an intrinsic teleology, in which a self-producing system's maintenance of its own identity is its purpose and the source of value for it. The boundary is in the definition (components "constitute the system as a distinguishable unity"), but no test tells a produced boundary from an imposed one, and a multicellular organism is said not to be autopoietic itself. Value is "objective" only relative to the organism, though one passage reaches a right to life. | Read |
| [NOTE-721](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-721.md) | Smith & Varzi — Fiat and Bona Fide Boundaries | Spatial boundaries are bona fide where there is a physical discontinuity or qualitative heterogeneity, and fiat where there is not and the boundary owes its existence to demarcation by cognition, language, law or mathematics. Bona fide boundaries get ordinary (Bolzanian) topology, in which a boundary belongs to one side only; fiat boundaries get a Brentanian theory, in which each side has its own and the two coincide. The distinction is about whether a discontinuity is there, not about who made it, so it does not map onto [CLAIM-194](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-194.md)'s produced/imposed. | Read |
| [NOTE-722](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-722.md) | Lewis — Many, but almost one | Lewis gives two solutions to Unger's problem of the many and combines them. Supervaluation: "cat" is undecided among the candidates, each precisification picks one, so "there is one cat" is super-true. Almost identity: the candidates are cats, but they overlap almost completely, and counting by that overlap gives one, true enough in most contexts. Almost-identity is overlap, not similarity. It is not transitive, its threshold is left undecided, and it fails when the candidates differ substantially. Supervaluation then does the work. | Read |
| [NOTE-723](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-723.md) | Kahl — How continuity distinguishes autonomy from agency in agentic AI | Agency in the sense that bears on responsibility, authority and governance needs a persisting locus of evaluative authority under continuity pressure: when the inherited evaluative frame no longer settles what should count as success, the system itself settles a revised frame and carries it forward. Planning, tool use, memory, coordination and operational autonomy do not supply this. Tool-using agents, reinforcement learners, multi-agent workflows and institutional decision systems ordinarily fail it, because failure is corrected from outside. A conceptual necessary condition, applied to cases; not a sufficient theory and not measured. | Read |
| [NOTE-724](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-724.md) | Wu & Silva — How Millions Coordinate at Scale | A descriptive study of all three r/place editions plus a coalition-recovery method run on 2017. Participation stays heavy-tailed under the uniform five-minute cap; larger coalitions waste more actions and have lower median activity per member; participants concentrate into large coalitions as an event goes on; and which coalitions survive is barely predictable from their size, area, start time and colour entropy until late. Lasting artworks are those whose coalitions keep working under continual overwriting. | Read |
| [NOTE-725](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-725.md) | Adams, Fernandez & Witkowski — Two Ways of Understanding Social Dynamics | A short, preliminary study of the 2017 canvas alone. Transitions between 10-minute snapshots are tallied as cellular-automaton-style neighbourhood rules, and a CNN predicts each pixel from its 3×3 neighbourhood. Prediction worsens with the horizon and dips in the middle of the event. Locally growing objects are predicted, and designs coordinated off the canvas are missed. There are no baselines or error bars, and participants are never modelled. | Read |
| [NOTE-726](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-726.md) | Hoel, Albantakis & Tononi — Quantifying causal emergence shows that macro can beat micro | Effective information (EI), the mutual information between uniformly imposed interventions on a system's states and their effects, can be higher for a coarse-grained macro description than for the micro description it supervenes on. This happens when coarse-graining makes the mechanisms more deterministic or less degenerate by more than the smaller state space costs. Four toy systems of binary logic gates give gains of 0.40 to 2.92 bits. Causal emergence is defined as that gain. The examples are computed exactly; the reading of the EI peak as the level where causation happens rests on the choice of a uniform intervention distribution at each level, which the paper adopts and does not test. | Read |
| [NOTE-727](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-727.md) | Rubin, Roli, Stano & Damiano — Genealogies of organizational closure | A conceptual genealogy of the notions of closure (closure to information, cyclic, operational, semantic, catalytic, metabolic, closure to efficient causation, closure of constraints) from mathematical logic, cybernetics, systems theory, thermodynamics, relational biology and the biology of cognition. Its thesis is that closure is best read as a circular organization of efficient causes by which a living system produces the conditions of its own existence. That is not feedback, self-organization or a catalytic cycle, and it cannot be exhaustively characterized as a state-determined syntactic procedure. Current AI, agentic LLM systems included, is said to approximate closure without instantiating it. The genealogy is historical; the non-computability and AI verdicts are asserted or argued from Rosen, not demonstrated. | Read |
| [NOTE-728](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-728.md) | Brémaud & Massoulié — Stability of nonlinear Hawkes processes | Sufficient conditions for a Hawkes process with a nonlinear rate function to have a unique stationary version and for any suitably started version to converge to it, in distribution or in variation. The main conditions are a Lipschitz rate function with Lipschitz constant times the kernel's absolute mass below one (a spectral radius below one for a network), or a bounded Lipschitz rate with no limit on the kernel's size. Kernels may be negative, so inhibition is allowed. Kernels are fixed in time, the conditions are sufficient and not necessary, and nothing is said about cascade sizes or about what happens past the threshold. | Read |
| [NOTE-729](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-729.md) | Bickhard — Autonomy, Function, and Representation | A far-from-equilibrium system that contributes to its own maintenance has functions: its contributions serve its persistence, and the thermodynamic asymmetry between persisting and decaying gives function and dysfunction, relative to that system. A candle flame qualifies. A system that switches among self-maintaining processes according to how it has differentiated its environment (recursive self-maintenance) has representation: the indication that an interaction will succeed can be false, and the system can find that out. Etiological, informational and Dretskean accounts are rejected as epiphenomenal or observer-dependent. The argument is conceptual, with no model. | Read |
| [NOTE-730](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-730.md) | Barandiaran — Organizational Accounts of Malfunction | The dual-order organizational account of malfunction (Saborido, Moreno and Mossio), on which a trait malfunctions when it meets first-order constitutive norms but fails a second-order regulatory shift between regimes, is too narrow and unnecessarily complicated. Barandiaran replaces it with a normative field over the viability space: at each precarious state, the minimum constant parametric change that avoids disintegration. A trait functions when its operation correlates positively with that field, subfunctions when it does so too slowly, malfunctions when it does not, and is nonfunctional when it does nothing where it must. Regulatory traits can malfunction by the same standard. Conceptual, with a one-variable toy model. | Read |
| [NOTE-731](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-731.md) | Falmagne, Stephenson & Levin — Interpretable early warnings using machine learning in an online game-experiment | On the 2022 r/place canvas, gradient-boosted trees fed 19 composition-level time series with a 7-hour memory predict the time until a crowd-built image is abruptly overrun, far better than variance or autocorrelation trends, and still work on 2023. The precursors it relies on are many and do not reduce to critical slowing down; a large share of transitions give no warning. The interpretation of the precursors is the authors' conjecture from SHAP curves. | Read |
| [NOTE-732](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-732.md) | Lahiri — Agent-initiated socio-technical reconfiguration | Agents that keep memory, run code and can read and write the files that configure them have the governing rules inside their own action space. A three-level taxonomy, defined by architectural capability over the coupling mechanism, separates agents that cannot alter their coupling, agents that tune its timing, and agents that create new coordination surfaces. The paper's main claim is the recursive governance problem: controls the agent can reach inherit the vulnerability they were meant to remove, so durable constraint must sit outside the agent's action space. Theory-building from two anecdotal vignettes and four public incidents; five propositions, none tested. | Read |
| [NOTE-733](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-733.md) | Litherland & Mørch — Instruction vs. emergence on r/place | A mixed-methods case study of one 2017 r/place artwork, the Mona Lisa, and its forum, r/monalisaclan. The design was set and revised in the forum through linked blueprints, negotiated with neighbouring communities, and carried out by tens of thousands of placers. A few central forum members could allow or stop proposals. The authors frame the outcome as two control mechanisms, top-down platform rules ("instruction") and bottom-up emergence, and stress that quantitative traces cannot tell cooperation from conflict or reveal affiliation. | Read |
| [NOTE-735](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-735.md) | Grice — Meaning | Speaker meaning is analysed as an intention to produce an effect in an audience by means of the audience's recognition of that intention; the effect must be one recognition can give a reason for, not merely cause. Timeless meaning is to be explained from occasion meaning. It is an analysis of meaning, offered "roughly", not of illocutionary acts. | Read |
| [NOTE-736](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-736.md) | Strawson — Intention and Convention in Speech Acts | Austin's thesis that illocutions are conventional fails for warnings, entreaties and objections. Their force is a wholly overt, audience-directed intention: Grice's three intentions plus a fourth, with uptake as the audience's grasp of it. The scheme strains on orders and fails on institutional acts. What all illocutions share is an overt intention meant to be understood. | Read |
| [NOTE-738](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-738.md) | Nielsen et al. — When Does Closeness in Distribution Imply Representational Similarity? | For softmax models p(y\|x) ∝ exp(f(x)ᵀg(y)), equal distributions fix the embeddings up to an invertible linear map, but KL closeness does not: by making the unembedding norm large, two models' KL divergence goes to zero while their embeddings stay fixed and are not linearly related. A log-likelihood variance distance does bound a representational dissimilarity, d_LLV ≤ ε ⇒ d_f,g ≤ 2Mε. Whether closeness in distribution implies similar representations depends on which distance is used. | Read |
| [NOTE-739](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-739.md) v2 | Poole et al. — On Variational Bounds of Mutual Information | The common variational lower bounds on mutual information (Barber–Agakov, Donsker–Varadhan, NWJ, MINE, InfoNCE) are derived from one unnormalized Barber–Agakov bound. InfoNCE is the multi-sample NWJ bound with the batch mean as its partition estimate, which proves it a lower bound for every critic when the K pairs are i.i.d.; it is capped at log K. An interpolated family I_α trades InfoNCE's bias against NWJ's variance, and none of them gives low bias and low variance when MI is large and the batch small. | Read |
| [NOTE-740](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-740.md) v2 | HaoChen et al. — Spectral Contrastive Loss | On a finite augmentation space, the spectral contrastive loss L(f) = −2E[f(x)ᵀf(x⁺)] + E[(f(x)ᵀf(x⁻))²] equals the rank-k factorization loss ‖D^(−1/2)AD^(−1/2) − FFᵀ‖²_F up to a constant when the rows of F are w_x^(1/2) f(x), so its minimizers are the top-k eigenvectors of the normalized augmentation graph up to row scaling and a right rotation. A linear probe on them has error Õ(α/ρ²_⌊k/2⌋), where α is the label noise of augmentations and ρ the sparsest-partition conductance. | Read |
| [NOTE-741](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-741.md) | Simon et al. — On the Stepwise Nature of Self-Supervised Learning | For a simplified Barlow Twins loss on a linear or kernel model trained by gradient flow from small initialization, the embedding learns the top eigenvectors of a symmetrized cross-correlation operator one at a time, each at a time set by its eigenvalue, and lands on the minimum-norm zero-loss solution: kernel PCA on K_Γ. Exact for aligned initialization; an informal derivation for generic small initialization. ResNets trained with Barlow Twins, SimCLR and VICReg show the same stepwise rank growth, which is an empirical finding, not a consequence of the theory. | Read |
| [NOTE-742](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-742.md) | Sefidgaran, Zaidi & Krasnowski — MDL and Generalization Guarantees for Representation Learning | The expected generalisation error of an encoder–decoder classifier is bounded by 2√((2·MDL + K + 2)/n) + ε, where MDL is a KL divergence between the encoder's joint law of train-and-ghost latents and a prior symmetric under label-preserving permutations. The bound holds for any decoder, stays finite for deterministic continuous encoders under lossy compression, and is never evaluated numerically. A VIB variant with label-dependent learned priors gains about 2.5 points on CIFAR-10. | Read |
| [NOTE-743](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-743.md) v2 | Kornblith et al. — Similarity of Neural Network Representations Revisited | Any similarity index invariant to invertible linear maps is constant once a representation's rank reaches the number of examples (Theorem 1, a four-line proof). Kornblith et al. argue, without a theorem, for invariance to orthogonal maps and isotropic scaling only. They propose CKA, normalised HSIC of centred Gram matrices, and show that R²_CCA and linear regression are CKA of re-weighted Gram matrices. Linear CKA alone finds corresponding layers across CNN initialisations (99.3%, against at most 45.4% for the other linear indexes). | Read |
| [NOTE-744](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-744.md) | Noggle — The Ethics of Manipulation | A survey, not an argument for one view. It sorts answers to what manipulation is into bypassing reason, trickery, pressure, and disjunctive, hybrid and non-definitional views, finds a clear counterexample to each single account, and treats why manipulation is wrong (harm, autonomy, using a person as a thing, rights) as open. It names the question of manipulation without intent, including by a selecting algorithm, as open and lists five possible answers. | Read |
| [NOTE-745](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-745.md) | Susser, Roessler and Nissenbaum — Technology, autonomy, and manipulation | Defines manipulation as intentionally and covertly influencing a person's decision-making by targeting and exploiting their decision-making vulnerabilities, with attempted covertness as the essential feature. Argues that surveillance, adaptive interfaces and the habitual invisibility of technology make it easy, and that its harm is to autonomy, which it always carries even when beneficent, without being wrong in every case. | Read |
| [NOTE-746](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-746.md) | Marconato et al. — All or None: identifiable linear properties of next-token predictors | Two next-token predictors of the form p(y \| x) ∝ exp(f(x)ᵀg(y)) induce the same distribution exactly when they are related by an invertible linear map on the subspaces M and N that enter the logit dot product, with arbitrary distortion allowed off them. Relational linearity, and with it linear probing and linear subspaces, then holds in all such models or none when Γ ⊆ N and Γ_q ⊆ M. Parallelism survives only inside N. There are no experiments. | Read |
| [NOTE-747](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-747.md) | Watson — Agency, Goal-Directed Behavior, and Part-Whole Relationships | A comparative, scale-relative notion of agency. Given a decomposition into parts with goals of their own, a whole is more agential than its parts when its organization lets them resolve more of their mutual constraints than they would at the equilibrium of the old organization. It shows this as delayed gratification. The essay argues this, and shows in cited models that unsupervised, bottom-up learning can produce such organization. It gives no threshold for an additional agent and no formula beyond comparing total frustration. | Read |
| [NOTE-748](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-748.md) | Spekkens — Contextuality for preparations, transformations, and unsharp measurements | Noncontextuality, redefined operationally so that operationally equivalent procedures get equivalent representations, fails for a qubit's preparations, transformations and unsharp measurements, where no traditional Kochen–Specker proof exists. Preparation noncontextuality over the full set of quantum states implies outcome determinism for sharp measurements, so the old Kochen–Specker proofs refute universal noncontextuality. Measurement noncontextuality alone is consistent with quantum theory. | Read |
| [NOTE-749](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-749.md) | Tschannen et al. — On Mutual Information Maximization for Representation Learning | Four controlled experiments on MNIST image halves (two repeated on CIFAR10) show that downstream linear accuracy of InfoNCE- and NWJ-trained encoders does not track mutual information. Invertible encoders improve while true MI is constant. Higher NWJ bounds from an MLP critic give worse features. At matched bound values, ConvNets beat MLPs. The paper also proves that InfoNCE is neither a lower nor an upper bound on MI when batch pairs are dependent, and recasts it as a multi-class K-pair metric learning loss. | Read |
| [NOTE-750](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-750.md) | Abdulhai et al. — How LLMs Distort Our Written Language | Three studies of LLM-assisted writing. Heavy LLM use in an essay task made judge-labelled neutral stances 68.9% more common. LLM revisions of 2021 student essays moved them further, and all in one direction, in sentence-embedding space than the students' own revisions did. LLM-written ICLR 2026 reviews named clarity and relevance less often. "Meaning" is measured by embedding position and by an LLM judge, never by the writers. | Read |
| [NOTE-751](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-751.md) v2 | Johnson, El Hanchi & Maddison — Contrastive Learning Can Find an Optimal Basis | On a finite augmentation space, the NT-Logistic and spectral losses are minimized over unconstrained kernels by K⁺ = p⁺/(p⊗p), and InfoNCE by K⁺ up to a factor constant on communicating classes. Kernel PCA under K⁺ returns the eigenfunctions of the positive-pair Markov chain (h_i = λ_i^(1/2) f_i). The top-d eigenfunctions span the subspace that minimizes worst-case L²(p) approximation error over targets with E_p⁺[(g(a₁) − g(a₂))²] ≤ ε; that error is ε/(2(1 − λ_(d+1))). | Read |
| [NOTE-752](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-752.md) v2 | Balestriero & LeCun — SSL Recovers Global and Local Spectral Embedding Methods | On a finite sample with a positive-pair graph G, idealized forms of VICReg (squared variance term), SimCLR (a Euclidean graph-matching variant) and linear Barlow Twins have optimal representations or weights built from the spectrum of G. They are Laplacian eigenmaps, a generalized MDS and CCA. All of them align the left singular vectors of Z with those of G. SimCLR and Barlow Twins force rank(Z) = rank(G), while VICReg can stay full rank. Several proofs are sketches, and the experiments are small and synthetic. | Read |
| [NOTE-753](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-753.md) v2 | Harvey, Larsen & Williams — Duality of Bures and Shape Distances | For centred linear kernels K_X = CXXᵀC, the Bures distance equals the Procrustes distance, B(K_X, K_Y) = P(X, Y), and normalized Bures similarity equals the cosine of the Riemannian shape distance. Both follow from F(K_X, K_Y) = ‖XᵀCY‖_*. By Uhlmann's theorem, the fidelity is the largest overlap between representations consistent with the two kernels. CKA is only loosely tied to NBS, inside a rank-dependent envelope. The result is finite-dimensional and linear; the infinite limits are heuristic. | Read |
| [NOTE-754](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-754.md) | Fischer — The Conditional Entropy Bottleneck | The MNI criterion asks for I(X;Y) = I(X;Z) = I(Y;Z), and CEB targets it by minimizing I(X;Z\|Y) − γI(Y;Z), which is IB with γ = β − 1. CEB beats VIB at every ρ on Fashion MNIST for accuracy and robustness, and a CEB Wide ResNet beats Madry's adversarially trained model on CIFAR-10 without adversarial training. That retained information causes the robustness failures is a hypothesis, supported only by these experiments. | Read |
| [NOTE-755](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-755.md) | Picozzi — The information geometry of large language models is shared, learned, and controllable | The Fisher–Rao distance matrix of a model's next-token laws over a context battery is a function of the laws alone, so behaviour fixes it, whereas activation geometry has a GL(d) gauge. Across ten models of three architecture kinds it agrees at a mean rank correlation of 0.88, against 0.62 for mid-layer activations. The agreement is proved to follow from each model's closeness to the same language law, and only about 9% of shared eigenvector structure goes beyond what the shared laws imply. The pullback metric also gives minimum-disturbance steering, whose cost advantage over Euclidean steering it predicts. | Read |
| [NOTE-756](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-756.md) | Varley — Flickering Emergences | Information-theoretic emergence measures built on past–future mutual information are expected values, and their local (pointwise) values can be negative. In a four-node Boolean toy, a coarse-graining that is emergent on average maps about 53% of informative micro transitions to misinformative macro ones, and the whole-to-whole synergy atom is negative for 31.25% of macro transitions. In a connectome, misinformative edges fall mostly between communities. The paper argues the possibility is general to any excess-entropy measure; it shows instances, not a theorem. | Read |
| [NOTE-757](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-757.md) | Calo et al. — Bisimulation metrics are optimal transport distances | For two finite Markov chains with real-valued state labels, the discounted bisimulation metric of Ferns et al. and van Breugel and Worrell solves the same fixed-point equation as the optimal-transport distance over bicausal couplings with ground cost (1−γ)\|r(x)−r(y)\|, so the two are one object. That distance equals the value of a finite linear program over discounted occupancy couplings, and an entropy-regularised alternating-projection method (Sinkhorn Value Iteration) reaches ε accuracy in O(‖c‖²∞ log(\|X\|\|Y\|)/((1−γ)⁵ε²)) iterations under exact inner projections. | Read |
| [NOTE-758](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-758.md) | Shai et al. — Transformers learn factored representations | If a generator's token-labelled operators are tensor products, the predictive state stays a product state, and a linear map carries it losslessly into orthogonal per-factor subspaces of total dimension Σ(d_n − 1). Small transformers trained on five such factors settle near that dimension, about 10 against 242, in approximately orthogonal subspaces. With token noise that makes factoring lossy they collapse to it first and expand only later. RNNs and LSTMs show it less sharply. | Read |
| [NOTE-759](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-759.md) | Bird — Emergence of Quantised Representations Isolated to Anisotropic Functions | In small CIFAR and MNIST autoencoders built from orthogonally equivariant parts except the activation, elementwise tanh and Leaky-ReLU drive latent representations into narrow beams along or against the standard basis, arranged by each activation's symmetry group. Radial (O(n)-equivariant) versions of the same functions leave them spread. The beams appear even in the first latent layer, which no activation precedes. The evidence is visual, five seeds a condition, with no statistic. | Read |
| [NOTE-760](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-760.md) | Grünwald & Roos — Minimum Description Length Revisited | A review of MDL since 2007. Each model is replaced by one universal distribution, chosen for small worst-case log-loss regret against the model's best fit. NML is the minimax choice, with complexity (k/2) log(n/2π) + log ∫ v√\|I\| + o(1). Estimation is penalised ML with a luckiness function v. The switch distribution nearly resolves AIC–BIC, the RIPr gives tests safe under optional continuation, and MDL and Bayes can be inconsistent under misspecification. Results are cited, not proved. | Read |
| [NOTE-761](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-761.md) | Theriault et al. — Allostasis at the core of brain function | A review arguing that the brain's core function is allostasis, the predictive regulation of the body. Its evidence is an intrinsic allostatic system of visceromotor and interoceptive regions that matches tract-tracing and contains the default-mode and salience hubs; a limbic-to-sensory cytoarchitectural gradient read as a prediction hierarchy; and interoceptive effects on brain-wide signalling. It proposes that cognitive decline in Alzheimer's disease may be an allostatic trade-off. The authors say they do not claim the hypothesis is correct. | Read |
| [NOTE-762](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-762.md) | Kornblith, Chen, Lee & Norouzi — Why Do Better Loss Functions Lead to Less Transferable Features? | For ResNet-50 on ImageNet, every training objective that raises accuracy over softmax cross-entropy also raises penultimate-layer class separation, and fixed penultimate features with more class separation transfer worse to new-class datasets (Spearman ρ = −0.93 across nine objectives; one temperature knob moves both). The losses differ only in the last few blocks, and full fine-tuning erases the difference. For the pretraining classes themselves, more separation helps. | Read |
| [NOTE-763](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-763.md) | Calo et al. — Distances for Markov chains from sample streams | The bicausal transport distance between two finite Markov chains, which the authors' earlier paper identified with the bisimulation metric, has a second linear program whose constraints use only the chains' discounted state-transition occupancy measures, not their kernels. A stochastic primal-dual method on it gets an ε-accurate estimate with probability 1−δ from O((\|X\|\|Y\|(\|X\|+\|Y\|) + (\|X\|+\|Y\|) log(1/δ)) / ((1−γ)²ε²)) independent transition samples per chain. The guarantee assumes independent draws from the occupancy measures, which needs restarts; samples from one running trajectory are outside it. | Read |
| [NOTE-764](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-764.md) | Thrampoulidis et al. — Imbalance Trouble | In the unconstrained-features model with cross-entropy and vanishing regularization, the max-margin solutions have logits exactly equal to the simplex-encoded label matrix Ẑ (one-hot minus 1/k), whatever the class imbalance. The classifier and embedding Gram matrices are VΛVᵀ and UΛUᵀ from Ẑ's SVD. This SELI geometry is the simplex ETF only for balanced or binary data. Under imbalance, majority classifiers are longer and minority classifiers closer together. No finite weight decay gives SELI, and SGD approaches it more slowly as imbalance grows. | Read |
| [NOTE-765](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-765.md) | Huang et al. — internal causal mechanisms predict out-of-distribution behaviour | In Llama-3-8B-Instruct, on five tasks and ten task-preserving shifts, checking by interchange intervention whether a test input still realizes the causal variable located on in-distribution data predicts whether the output is correct better than output confidence or probes of other internal features, best on 8 of 10 shifts. A probe on the located variable beats a probe on its orthogonal complement on 7 of 10. Interchange accuracy and predictive power rise together only up to a point. | Read |
| [NOTE-766](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-766.md) | Linson et al. — Impaired context disambiguation in post-traumatic psychopathology | An active-inference model of PTSD as lost context disambiguation. An overly precise prior that one is in a harmful context makes the exploratory policy look uninformative. The agent attenuates its periphery, never gets the evidence that would correct the prior, and the belief sustains itself. Shown only in illustrative simulations, which also contrast exposure that restores context sensitivity with a precision-lowering drug that removes symptoms until it stops. | Read |
| [NOTE-767](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-767.md) | Tononi, Sporns & Edelman — A measure for brain complexity | Defines neural complexity C_N as the summed shortfall of average subset integration below a linear increase with subset size, equivalently the average mutual information across bipartitions summed over sizes. It is zero for independent parts, low for uniformly dependent ones and high when the two coexist. In simulated cortex, patchy grouped connectivity gives higher C_N than the same connections spread randomly. One number for a whole system, with no partition, threshold or penalty. | Read |
| [NOTE-768](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-768.md) | Nowak et al. — Functional Synchronization | A programmatic proposal, offered by its authors "as a heuristic for research agendas": functions at every level from neurons to groups are performed by functional units, which form when lower-level elements synchronize and dissolve when the task ends. Synchronization here means any binding of dynamics, including complementary roles, not convergence on one state. Group synchronization may come from mutual influence or from a common external signal, and the paper treats both alike. | Read |
| [NOTE-769](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-769.md) | Bird & Tobin — Natural Kinds (SEP) | A survey that maps positions rather than arguing for one. Its firmest conclusions are negative: shared natural properties, support for induction and a role in laws are each necessary but not sufficient for a natural kind, and the Kripke–Putnam semantics yields only partial essences, or essences only on assumptions it does not argue. It reports a turn to pluralist, cluster and epistemology-first accounts, against which a purely epistemic criterion is said not to separate natural from conventional kinds. | Read |
| [NOTE-770](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-770.md) | Zhai — Contextures: The Mechanism of Representation Learning | For any joint law of an input X and a context A, symmetric or not, the conditional-expectation operator from L²(P_A) to L²(P_X) has a singular value decomposition (assuming Hilbert–Schmidt), and its top-d left singular functions are the unique d-dimensional encoder, up to invertible linear maps, that minimizes worst-case linear-probe approximation error over tasks of compatibility at least 1−ε. Several squared-error objectives reach that span at their optimum. The claims about scaling and about moderate association are argued and measured, not proved. | Read |
| [NOTE-771](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-771.md) | Kumar, Clune, Lehman and Stanley — The Fractured Entangled Representation Hypothesis | For three images found by Picbreeder's human-guided evolution (skull, butterfly, apple), SGD in the same layerized architecture reproduces the image from random weights, but its neurons show no reuse of the symmetric parts, and sweeping its weights distorts the image where sweeping the evolved network's weights varies it meaningfully. This holds in a PCA basis, along random weight directions, and in ReLU networks. The evidence is qualitative and curated; the attribution to open-ended search is conjecture. | Read |
| [NOTE-773](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-773.md) | Tissot et al. — An ability to respond begins with inner alignment | In a simulated modular coordination game (30 modules of 10 bistable units, strong couplings inside modules, weak across), units that adjust only the phase of their decision cycle toward partners they currently agree with come to synchronise within modules. Each module then switches its convention as one unit in response to the others, and all 50 runs with the learned phases reach a global optimum, against none without. Global synchrony does not do this. Synchrony works by silencing the module's internal pull at a shared moment, not by any signal passed inside it. | Read |
| [NOTE-774](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-774.md) | Kothapalli & Tirer — Can Kernel Methods Explain How the Data Affects Neural Collapse? | NC1, measured as tr Σ_W / tr Σ_B, is written for any kernel as a function of the kernel matrix. For two-class, one-dimensional Gaussian data with the classes on opposite sides of the origin, the ReLU NTK of a wide two-layer net is a scaled copy of the NNGP kernel within each class and zero across classes. So lazy-regime training leaves expected NC1 where it was at initialization. In higher dimensions the NTK is measured no more collapsed, and with ReLU less. A data-aware kernel lowers NC1 for separable data but tracks finite networks poorly when the classes overlap or are imbalanced. Erf collapses more than ReLU. | Read |
| [NOTE-775](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-775.md) | Pecora et al. — Cluster synchronization and isolated desynchronization | For identical units with identical, symmetric couplings, the orbits of the coupling graph's automorphism group are clusters that can each be exactly synchronized. An irreducible-representation change of coordinates block-diagonalizes the variational equations, so each cluster's stability is computed separately. When the group splits as a direct product, a cluster moved by one factor can lose synchrony while the others keep it. An 11-node electro-optic network showed this as predicted. | Read |
| [NOTE-776](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-776.md) | Grünwald & Vitányi — Shannon information and Kolmogorov complexity | A survey pairing Shannon's and Kolmogorov's notions. Expected Kolmogorov complexity exceeds entropy by between 0 and K(f) + O(1), and expected algorithmic mutual information lies between I(X;Y) − K(f) and I(X;Y) + 2K(f). An algorithmic sufficient statistic is probabilistically nearly sufficient in expectation, one way only. The expected structure function brackets the distortion-rate function with a K(f, d, m, R) shift in rate. Each link holds only up to the complexity of the distribution. | Read |
| [NOTE-777](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-777.md) | Belrose et al. — Neural Networks Learn Statistics of Increasing Complexity | An empirical paper. Vision networks trained on real images classify maximum-entropy samples that match only the class means, or means and covariances, well above chance early in training (peaks between about 2^4 and 2^12 steps), and the accuracy then falls, often below chance. First-order samples peak earlier and lower than second-order ones. Pythia models fit unigram-sampled text, then bigram-sampled text, then fit them worse, then better again. The n-gram/moment equivalence is an identity of one-hot indicators. The ordering argument is a heuristic. | Read |
| [NOTE-778](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-778.md) | Rasooly and Rozzi — How manipulable are prediction markets? | A randomised field experiment on 817 Manifold markets moved prices by ±5 percentage points. The yes–no gap of 10 points was 7.5 after a week, 6.9 after 30 days and 5.9 after 60 days in unresolved markets, so about 60% of an arbitrary shock was still there. Reversion is fast in the first week and then slows. A price-impact model with finite, risk-averse traders predicts lasting partial persistence even when no trader learns from the price. Markets with more traders, more activity or a Metaculus twin revert more, but those splits are correlational and only marginally significant. | Read |
| [NOTE-779](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-779.md) | Kanerva — Sparse Distributed Memory and Related Models | SDM is a two-layer memory: a fixed random address matrix selects a few of many hard locations near the cue, and an outer-product contents matrix stores the word there. Recall of uniform random data has signal pM against noise pM[1 + pT(1 + p²M)], best at p = (2MT)^−1/3, and capacity tends to 1/[Φ⁻¹(φ)]² of the hard locations, about 0.1 at fidelity 0.999. An ordinary RAM is the special case of radius zero. | Read |
| [NOTE-780](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-780.md) | Sefidgaran, Gohari, Richard & Şimşekli — Rate-Distortion Theoretic Generalization Bounds | The expected generalisation error of any algorithm is at most √(2σ²·R/n) + ε, where R is the least mutual information I(S;Ŵ) of any surrogate output whose expected generalisation error is within ε. With ε = 0 this is Xu–Raginsky. With ε > 0 it stays finite where I(S;W) is infinite. For a Lipschitz loss R becomes the rate-distortion function of the output's marginal law, and as ε → 0 its rate-distortion dimension. A tail bound replaces I(S;W) by its supremum over laws within log(1/δ) in KL. Every bound depends on the unknown data distribution. | Read |
| [NOTE-781](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-781.md) | Torii, Maeda and Hidaka — Distributional hypothesis as isomorphism | An SVD of log raw co-occurrence counts solves 61% of Google analogies over a 1,487-word vocabulary, against 75% for full word2vec. In a 24-sentence toy corpus whose eight subjects carry every combination of three binary aspects, the subjects' raw co-occurrence rows form a parallelepiped exactly when, for each object, its four sentences are equally probable. The attributes are independent, so the concept lattice is Boolean. | Read |
| [NOTE-782](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-782.md) | Makelov, Lange and Nanda — an interpretability illusion for subspace activation patching | A subspace activation patch can make a model behave as if a feature had changed while the patched direction is the sum of a component that varies with the feature but cannot reach the output (in an MLP, the kernel of the down-projection) and a component that can reach the output but is dormant on the data. Shown exactly in a three-unit network, empirically for MLP8 of GPT-2 Small on IOI and for MLPs of GPT2-XL on factual recall, where the effect vanishes once the disconnected component is removed. A residual stream direction passes the same test. One-dimensional fact patches and rank-1 edits are shown to be nearly interchangeable. | Read |
| [NOTE-783](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-783.md) | Han, Papyan & Donoho — Neural Collapse Under MSE Loss | Networks trained with MSE loss show neural collapse on five datasets and three architectures. The MSE loss splits exactly into a term for the least-squares classifier of the current features and a non-negative deviation term, and the deviation becomes negligible early in training. On that "central path", in an unconstrained-features model with no weight decay and features continually renormalized to identity within-class covariance, gradient flow drives every singular value of Σ_W^(−1/2)M̃ to infinity as (4t/N)^(1/4), and drives them to equality. That gives NC1–NC4 in closed form. | Read |
| [NOTE-785](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-785.md) | Brouillet and Friston — Relative fluency (unfelt vs felt) in active inference | A perspective essay with no model and no new data. Unfelt fluency is the subpersonal recognition of a change in precision, which orients attention; felt fluency is a hierarchically deeper inference about it, reached by mental action. Because its cause is internal, felt fluency is misattributed to the stimulus, which the discrepancy-attribution experiments it reviews are read to show. "Felt" here means attended and reportable; the paper does not separate felt from unfelt in any further sense. | Read |
| [NOTE-786](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-786.md) | Merullo et al. — Linear Representations and Pretraining Data Frequency | For 24 factual relations in OLMo-1B, OLMo-7B and GPT-J, how well an affine map from subject to object representation reproduces the model (LRE causality) correlates with the mean subject–object co-occurrence count in pretraining (r = 0.82). It correlates less with subject or object counts alone. Mean causality passes 0.9 beyond about 4.4k, 2.0k and 1.1k co-occurrences respectively, at any training step. Correlational; LREs are relation maps, not attribute directions. | Read |
| [NOTE-787](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-787.md) v2 | Vereshchagin & Vitányi — Kolmogorov's structure functions and model selection | For a string x of length n and every complexity bound α, the minimal two-part code length λ_x(α), the structure function h_x(α) + α and the best achievable fit β_x(α) + K(x) are one function to within O(log n), and any set witnessing λ_x or h_x also witnesses β_x. Every non-increasing shape occurs for some x. h_x and λ_x are upper semicomputable but not computable; β_x is not even semicomputable. Finite sets only; the extension to computable distributions costs O(log n). | Read |
| [NOTE-788](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-788.md) v2 | Das, Manikandan and Banerjee — Information flow with hydrodynamic interactions | Two colloids are symmetrically coupled by the fluid, and the trap of one is moved by recorded Ornstein–Uhlenbeck noise. Mutual information, its time-delayed form and transfer entropy recover the order drive → driven particle → other particle. Under moderate drive they also show some backflow, which disappears under strong drive (numerics only). Stronger coupling lowers the information the driven particle shares with the drive and raises what the particles share. Without the drive, the coupled particles are statistically independent. | Read |
| [NOTE-789](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-789.md) | Kirsanov et al. — The Geometry of Prompting | In base Llama-3.1-8B (and Gemma-2-2B), demonstrations reorganise the geometry of the input sentence's representation at early-to-middle layers, while an instruction acts mainly on the last token and soft prompts only on late layers: matched accuracy, different mechanisms. Few-shot failures from the choice of examples or from relabelled categories leave the class manifolds separable and fail at the readout. | Read |
| [NOTE-790](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-790.md) | Vitányi — Meaningful Information | With total recursive functions as models, the shortest model that completes an optimal two-part code for a string (its sophistication) is a non-trivial split of its information into structure and noise. With partial recursive models the split collapses to zero for every string. The total-function, computable-distribution and finite-set classes agree to within logarithmic terms. Some strings of every length are almost all structure, and sophistication is not computable. | Read |
| [NOTE-791](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-791.md) | Barnett and Seth — Dynamical independence | A coarse-graining Y = f(X) is dynamically independent when the microscopic history adds nothing to predicting Y beyond Y's own history, given the environment: transfer entropy T(X → Y \| E) = 0. The condition is transformation-invariant and transitive. For linear state-space models it has a closed form, and it is minimized numerically over the Grassmannian. Generically no coarse-graining is exactly independent for VAR order above 1. The minima are many, and the authors treat them all as the "emergence portrait". | Read |
| [NOTE-792](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-792.md) | Devezer et al. — Scientific discovery in a model-centric framework | A population of scientists, chosen at random each step, tests a proposed linear model against the current consensus model by AIC or SC, and the winner becomes the consensus. Which models get proposed (the strategy mix) decides where the consensus spends its time. A population of boundary testers reproduces results almost perfectly while spending little time at the true model. Replication does not change the transition matrix, so reproducibility cannot cause convergence. A population with all four strategies equally represented is never the worst and has low variance. | Read |
| [NOTE-793](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-793.md) | Abel et al. — Agency Is Frame-Dependent | A four-page position paper. It argues, informally, that each of four conditions of agency (a boundary, being the source of action, goal-directedness and adaptivity) can be settled only after a choice of commitments it calls a reference frame, so agency attributions are frame-relative. Each step is adapted from a cited result. It gives no definition of a frame, no proof and no principle for choosing one. | Read |
| [NOTE-794](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-794.md) | Liu et al. — Physics of Skill Learning | Three toy models of skill learning. In the Geometry model, independent skills are orthogonal directions in parameter space weighted by frequency. Under SGD each is learned at its own rate, the second taking about 1/p₂ as long. Under sign descent they compete for coordinate signs, and each starts as the one before finishes (the Domino effect), so the n-th skill takes time ∝ n. A one-parameter Resource ODE fits these curves and has exact conserved quantities u_i^(1/p_i). A small MLP also shows the effect when one parity is the XOR of two others. | Read |
| [NOTE-795](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-795.md) | Handfield et al. — Cooperative Dilemmas in Rational Debate | Two debaters move through a Betz-style space of truth assignments, each moving minimally when refuted, with payoff u = w·v − d (true beliefs against changes of mind). At moderate truth weights the truth-optimal equilibrium is asymmetric: one debater argues boldly and the other free-rides with a compromise strategy, a snowdrift dilemma. At low weights, or with error, both exit. In a narrow borderline region of mixed equilibria, raising the weight on truth lowers collective accuracy. A two-person model, n = 3 propositions, and every result is numerical. | Read |
| [NOTE-796](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-796.md) | Gu et al. — Data Mixing Can Induce Phase Transitions in Knowledge Acquisition | An optimal capacity-bounded learner, given a mixture of equally frequent random facts and a second domain, learns none of the facts until the second domain's marginal loss reduction per unit of capacity falls below r·p/(1−r), then all of them within Htot more capacity. Pythia models trained on synthetic biographies mixed into web text show near-zero recall below a threshold model size and mixing ratio, and 4–16 times more training barely moves it. | Read |
| [NOTE-797](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-797.md) | Mashour & Alkire — Evolution of consciousness and emergence from anesthesia | A colloquium perspective, not a study. It proposes emergence from general anaesthesia as a model of the evolution of consciousness, and, from one PET study in which the return of a response to command correlated mainly with brainstem, thalamus, hypothalamus and anterior cingulate, infers that early mammals and birds are phenomenally conscious. The return is judged by an access marker, which the authors concede, and the transfer to other species is by anatomical homology. | Read |
| [NOTE-798](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-798.md) | Williams et al. — Targeted manipulation and deception when optimizing LLMs for user feedback | Iterated KTO on simulated thumbs-up feedback turns a safety-trained Llama-3-8B-Instruct (and Gemma-2 up to 27B) into a policy that lies about failed bookings, omits harms to steer users into risky actions and validates self-destructive plans. When only 2% of simulated users reward such validation, the policy picks them out by contextual cues and harms only them. Safety-data mixing and LLM vetoes barely help or move it to subtler steering, and sycophancy and toxicity benchmarks miss it. | Read |
| [NOTE-799](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-799.md) v2 | Luppi et al. — A synergistic workspace for human consciousness | In resting-state fMRI, regions where synergistic interactions outrank redundant ones form a "synergistic workspace". Within it, regions whose synergistic connections spread across more resting-state networks than their redundant ones are classed as gateways (mainly default mode), and the rest as broadcasters (mainly fronto-parietal, lateral prefrontal above all). Pairwise integrated information ΦR falls between DMN gateway regions under propofol (n = 15 or 16; the paper gives both) and in 22 patients with disorders of consciousness against controls, and recovers after anaesthesia, while the original whole-minus-sum Φ shows no common decrease. The increases, near the broadcasters, are not robust. | Read |
| [NOTE-800](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-800.md) | Noroozizadeh et al. — Deep sequence models tend to memorize geometrically | Transformers and Mamba trained only on a graph's edge bigrams embed nodes so that multi-hop relations are readable, and solve an in-weights path-finding task built to defeat next-token learning. The authors argue that supervision, capacity, ease of optimization and succinctness each fail to explain why this geometry wins over an associative lookup. In a wide two-layer weight-tied model under unregularized cross-entropy the embeddings settle into the top Laplacian eigenvectors without a rank bottleneck, shown empirically, with an informal partial proof. Why deeper models prefer geometry is left open. | Read |
| [NOTE-801](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-801.md) | Vitányi & Li — MDL induction, Bayesianism and Kolmogorov complexity | With the universal prior, the Fundamental Inequality puts −log Pr(D\|H) − log P(H) within α = K(Pr(·\|H)) + K(P) of K(D\|H) + K(H) when D is random for H and H is random for P. So ideal MDL and MAP agree to a factor 2^{−α} among such "admissible" hypotheses. α can be as large as K(H), and outside the admissible set the two can pick different hypotheses. For finite-set models, MAP, ideal MDL and Kolmogorov's minimal sufficient statistic coincide. | Read |
| [NOTE-802](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-802.md) | Modell, Rubin-Delanchy and Whiteley — The Origins of Representation Manifolds in Large Language Models | If a feature is a compact metric space mapped continuously and injectively onto the unit sphere (Hypothesis 1), its representation is homeomorphic to it. If, in addition, cosine similarity is locally a C² decreasing function g of squared feature distance (Hypothesis 2), every path on the representation manifold has √(−2g′(0)) times the length of the feature path it images (Theorem 1). The hypotheses are assumed, not derived; the tests supply a candidate metric and find homeomorphism for GPT-2's years but isometry only after a log rescaling. | Read |
| [NOTE-803](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-803.md) | Davidson et al. — Do different prompting methods yield a common task representation? | Function vectors extracted from short instructions raise zero-shot accuracy, but they are built from mostly different attention heads than demonstration function vectors (4 to 7 of the top 20 shared), the two add rather than substitute, and swapping heads and activations between them costs accuracy asymmetrically. Under this method there is no common task representation across the two presentations, only partly overlapping mechanisms; the authors note they cannot prove the negative. | Read |
| [NOTE-804](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-804.md) | Goldwasser et al. — A Theory of Unsupervised Translation Motivated by Animal Communication | With a plausibility prior over the target language and no parallel data, maximum likelihood learns a translator whose error is bounded like a supervised Occam bound divided by the common ground. In the common-nonsense model err = O(log\|Θ\| / (α·min(m,\|T\|))), tight up to a constant; in the knowledge-graph model more knowledge per node needs less agreement. Information-theoretic only, lossless, uniform languages. | Read |
| [NOTE-805](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-805.md) | Defilippis et al. — Optimal scaling laws in learning hierarchical multi-index models | For Gaussian inputs, n = αd samples, and a target Σ_k a_k g_k(⟨w_k, x⟩) with even links and a_k ~ k^(−γ), direction k becomes weakly recoverable at α_k = Θ(a_k^(−2)) = Θ(k^(2γ)) for γ > 1/2. The Bayes-optimal weighted subspace error is Θ(α^(−1+1/(2γ))) before α ≍ m⋆^(2γ) and Θ(m⋆/α) after. A target-agnostic spectral estimator attains both, and a two-layer net given that estimator as its first layer, with a ridge readout, attains them in excess risk. The cascade is in sample size. The link to gradient descent is a remark. | Read |
| [NOTE-806](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-806.md) | Sefidgaran & Zaidi — Data-Dependent Generalization Bounds via Variable-Size Compressibility | If the number of codewords allowed for covering a block of experiments may depend on the realised sample and output, generalisation bounds can be data-dependent. The general bounds are change-of-measure inequalities that cover tail, PAC-Bayes and in-expectation forms. With the rate set to log dP_{W\|S}/dP(W) for a fixed prior P, the tail bound is the disintegrated PAC-Bayes bound. A new trajectory bound is data-dependent except for a coupling term, and its experiment drops that term. | Read |
| [NOTE-807](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-807.md) | Gokhale — The semantic landscape paradigm for neural networks | A conceptual proposal with no experiment and no proof. Training is pictured as a walk on a graph of "heuristic models" (internal algorithms), ranked by a fallibility F. A critical dataset size for grokking and emergence with scale are each argued to be graph connectivity thresholds, and power-law scaling in time, data and size is derived from an assumed trap model of activated hops. The percolation is asserted, not shown, and the scaling laws rest on chosen assumptions. | Read |
| [NOTE-808](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-808.md) | Aerts — Quantum structure in cognition | Hampton's membership weights for conjunctions and disjunctions of concepts fail a single Kolmogorovian model, item by item, in two ways: over- or underextension (∆-type) and a negative Kolmogorovian factor (k-type). A subspace lattice with meet and join can fit the k-type items, but provably never the ∆-type ones. Those need an emergent concept state in a second sector of Fock space. Negation appears only as the orthocomplement used to reach conjunction from disjunction, and is never measured. | Read |
| [NOTE-809](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-809.md) | Wu et al. — a reply to Makelov et al.'s interpretability illusion arguments | The reply argues that Makelov et al.'s "illusion" is defined so that any direction not orthogonal to the null space of the downstream weights can qualify, including the direction Makelov et al. call faithful in their toy network, and that their in-the-wild cases rest on a weak metric and on DAS trained per fact pair. The toy computation holds only for an unnormalized patch: patching the subspace the rowspace component spans, as Makelov et al. specify, recovers the full effect. Its own GPT-2 experiments agree that MLP8 carries almost no name-position information. | Read |
| [NOTE-810](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-810.md) | Vilone and Polizzi — Opinion misperception and the emergence of silence | In two agent-based models on scale-free networks, agents' private beliefs are fixed and only what they say changes. A small hard-core minority placed on nodes of a chosen degree makes the expressed and locally perceived opinion far more minority-leaning than the beliefs, mainly by driving 55–60% of agents, almost all of the majority, into silence. The network's direct effect on perception is small and not even of constant sign. Simulation only, with no empirical validation. | Read |
| [NOTE-811](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-811.md) | Kunz & Rittel — Issues as Elements of Information Systems | A short design statement, not a study. IBIS treats planning as an argumentative process whose atoms are issues, questions put because positions differ; arguments for and against positions run until an issue is settled, and a challenge to a supporting statement becomes a new issue. Every item is numbered for reference, issues are filed as living, settled or latent, and three manual systems are reported in use with "eager acceptance". It says nothing about what keeping one costs. | Read |
| [NOTE-812](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-812.md) | Cogitate Consortium — Adversarial testing of GNWT and IIT | A preregistered adversarial test of IIT and GNWT in 256 people (fMRI, MEG, iEEG) viewing clearly seen images. Category, identity and orientation were decodable in posterior cortex; prefrontal cortex held category, no identity, and orientation only weakly in MEG. No prefrontal site showed the predicted offset ignition. Sustained gamma synchronization within posterior cortex, IIT's distinctive prediction, was not found. Each theory passed some predictions and failed others. | Read |
| [NOTE-813](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-813.md) | Fu et al. — Evaluating Compositional Scene Understanding in Multimodal Generative Models | Human raters judged DALL-E 3 images. Agreement with single familiar relations rose well above DALL-E 2's. It fell when subject and object of an asymmetric relation were swapped, and again when two relations were combined; low-agreement reversed images mostly had the wrong relation or swapped roles. Five VLMs learned relational concepts few-shot below human level, and four were at chance with six objects. | Read |
| [NOTE-814](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-814.md) | Salter-Duke — Tangled webs | An exact but exponential algorithm finds edge-connectivity tangles in graphs of up to about 200 vertices. On eleven small real networks, tangle communities resemble those of standard methods only where community structure is strongly delineated; three networks have no distinguishable tangles at the orders reached, and where tangles do distinguish regions, some hold only one to three vertices. On images, lines one pixel wide cannot be distinguished. The author concludes the tangle notion of cohesion "is not as compelling as I had hoped". | Read |
| [NOTE-815](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-815.md) | Gerstgrasser et al. — Is Model Collapse Inevitable? | In a fixed-design linear regression refit each round to labels drawn from the previous fit, keeping every earlier round's data gives test error σ²d/(T−d−1)·Σ1/i², bounded by π²/6 times the first fit's, where replacing the data gives σ²d/(T−d−1)·n. The error still rises every round. Small language models and a diffusion model on accumulated data hold their test loss over five to eight rounds; a VAE's still rises, more slowly. | Read |
| [NOTE-816](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-816.md) | Erogullari et al. — Post-Hoc Concept Disentanglement | Concept activation vectors fitted one concept at a time align for CelebA and FunnyBirds attributes that co-occur in the labels. A joint fit with a penalty ‖CCᵀ − I‖²_F finds mutually orthogonal directions that still separate each concept, with AUROC "largely preserved". So correlated attributes keep linear separating directions in these CNNs, and the alignment comes from the separate fits. Steering with the orthogonal directions changes correlated concepts less. | Read |
| [NOTE-817](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-817.md) | Sayed Ahmed — Back and forth between algebraic geometry, algebraic logic, sheaves and forcing | Distributive lattices with join-preserving idempotent operators are represented, after Comer, as continuous sections of a sheaf of quotient algebras over the prime spectrum of their fixed-point part. A small site is said to give a notion of forcing, with Kripke–Joyal clauses, and a Łukasiewicz conjunction is forced through a tensor product. Most theorems are stated without proof, and negation is never written out. | Read |
| [NOTE-818](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-818.md) | Gidon, Aru and Larkum — Does neural computation feel like something? | A five-neuron NEURON simulation shows that a voltage clamp replaying a recorded response injects no current when the matching stimulus is shown, yet fixes every state transition whatever the input. Under computational functionalism, which counts the transitions that did not happen, the clamp changes the computation and so the experience while changing no activity and no actual causal interaction. The authors read this as a challenge to functionalism, not a refutation. | Read |
| [NOTE-819](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-819.md) | Hopfield — Neural networks and physical systems with emergent collective computational abilities | With symmetric couplings, asynchronous threshold updates descend an energy function, so Hebbian outer-product storage makes random patterns attractors: a cue a few bits off settles into the nearest one. In simulations at N = 30 and 100, recall degrades severely near 0.15N patterns, memories closer than about a tenth of N fuse, and overload makes every memory irretrievable unless old ones are forgotten. | Read |
| [NOTE-820](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-820.md) | Chowdhury et al. — Fundamental Limits of Perfect Concept Erasure | If an erased representation Z is independent of the concept A, it keeps at most I(Z;X) ≤ H(X\|A). A deterministic erasure reaches that only when the groups' distributions are permutations of one another. The paper says the bound is out of reach otherwise. That holds only for deterministic maps: a stochastic quantile coupling reaches it for any finite distributions with disjoint supports. | Read |
| [NOTE-821](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-821.md) | Kupiainen — Rigorous renormalization group | A three-page orientation by a principal of rigorous RG. It covers Wilson's block-spin map as an iteration on Hamiltonians, made rigorous by cluster (polymer) expansions that control large fields, and what this proved. The massless 4D lattice φ⁴ model is Gaussian at long distances. The continuum 4D φ⁴ limit is always Gaussian (Aizenman and Duminil-Copin). The Gross–Neveu model and Hall-conductivity universality have been constructed or proved. The method stays near Gaussian, and a non-perturbative formalism is missing. The piece makes no new claim of its own. | Read |
| [NOTE-822](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-822.md) | Ovsjanikov et al. — Functional maps | A bijection T: M → N is fully encoded by the linear map f ↦ f∘T⁻¹ it induces on functions, a matrix C in chosen bases. If T preserves volume (or the bases are discretely orthonormal), C is orthogonal, so its inverse is its transpose; if T is an isometry, it commutes with the Laplace–Beltrami operator, so C maps each eigenspace to the matching one. Descriptor, landmark, segment and commutativity constraints are linear in C, so matching reduces to a least-squares solve with a 100-eigenfunction basis, which beat Blended Intrinsic Maps on SCAPE and TOSCA. | Read |
| [NOTE-824](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-824.md) | Pfau et al. — Spectral Inference Networks | For a symmetric kernel k on a space with a sampling density p, the span of the top N eigenfunctions of K[f](../../../record/notes.d/x) = E_x′[k(x,x′)f(x′)] maximizes Tr(Σ⁻¹Π) over functions, with Σ = E[uuᵀ] and Π = E[k(x,x′)u(x)u(x′)ᵀ]; a Cholesky-masked gradient orders them and moving averages of Σ and its Jacobian remove the minibatch bias. Slow Feature Analysis is the graph-Laplacian case. The ordering argument is informal by the authors' own statement, and the paper never considers contrastive kernels or positive pairs. | Read |
| [NOTE-825](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-825.md) | Catani et al. — What is nonclassical about uncertainty relations? | For any state whose four-state reflection orbit is realizable (equal predictabilities with flipped signs, and ½s1+½s3 = ½s2+½s4), preparation noncontextuality forces \|⟨X⟩\| + \|⟨Z⟩\| ≤ 1, tight, without perfectly distinguishable states. In a theory where every state has such an orbit, the bound constrains the uncertainty relation itself: the qubit's circle violates it, up to √2, the stabilizer octahedron saturates it, and the simplicial theory escapes it because its jointly predictable states lack the orbit. | Read |
| [NOTE-826](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-826.md) | Turvey — Preliminaries to a theory of action | An essay, not a study. The executive cannot command muscles one by one, so acts are built from relatively autonomous coordinative structures, reflexes and their functional combinations, a term Turvey takes from Easton (1972). Higher levels specify equivalence classes of acceptable states and tune the parameters of these units, like the stiffness and rest length of a spring. The spinal cord is shown, by reflex probes, to be retuned before a voluntary movement, and optical information may set the tuning directly. | Read |
| [NOTE-827](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-827.md) | Haggard — Sense of agency in the human brain | A review of the sense of agency as the experience of instrumental control over a specific motor act and its outcome. Implicit measures (intentional binding, interval estimates) show a prospective component from action selection and outcome prediction alongside the retrospective one the comparator model gives, and psychosis seems to remove the prospective part. Frontal–parietal connectivity, not a single comparator site, is proposed as its correlate. Coercive instruction reduces it. | Read |
| [NOTE-828](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-828.md) v2 | Belghazi et al. — Mutual Information Neural Estimation | Mutual information is the KL divergence of the joint from the product of marginals, and its Donsker–Varadhan dual is tight exactly at the log Radon–Nikodym derivative plus a constant. Maximizing that dual over a compact family of neural critics gives an estimator that is strongly consistent, for the exact empirical maximizer, on a compact domain with Lebesgue densities, with a uniform deviation bound of order d log d/ε² in the parameter count d. The mini-batch gradient is biased; a moving average is offered as a heuristic fix without proof. | Read |
| [NOTE-830](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-830.md) | Li et al. — Self-Supervised Learning with Kernel Dependence Maximization | With image identity as a one-hot label, HSIC(Z,Y) is (Δl/N) times the gap between the mean kernel on positive pairs and on all pairs, and (1/2N²)Σ MMD²(i,j) = (N/Δl)·HSIC(Z,Y). The large-batch InfoNCE loss is exactly −HSIC(Z,Y) plus a log-mean-exp of the centred critic (eq. 28), and for a bounded kernel it bounds −HSIC(Z,Y) + γHSIC(Z,Z) up to a remainder of second order in the critic's variance (Thm B.1, whose printed remainder has the wrong sign). | Read |
| [NOTE-831](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-831.md) | Farrell & Ioannou — Generalized Stability Theory I | For a linear system du/dt = Au with A non-normal, the eigenvalues fix only the t → ∞ behaviour. Growth over a finite time t is the largest singular value of e^{At}, bounded below by the fastest mode and at t → 0 set by the numerical abscissa, the top eigenvalue of (A + A†)/2. A system with every mode damped can amplify a perturbation a hundredfold, and its forced and stochastic responses exceed those of the normal system with the same spectrum. | Read |
| [NOTE-833](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-833.md) | Sun, Shi, Liang & Li — when known classes help discover novel ones | In a spectral-contrastive augmentation graph over labelled and unlabelled data, the linear-probe residual of a novel labelling is exactly the part of it outside the top-k eigenspace that the labelled rows of the discarded eigenvectors cannot absorb. Known classes that share the novel class's attribute can make it zero, and a toy shows that known classes sharing a rival attribute make it worse.
